Myth beat. Chisullyeong ridge. ONE device: a woman’s standing body turning into a dark stone upright against bare paper. FACE from the attached Chisul portrait translated into a few ink strokes — fifties, lined, wooden binyeo, looking east — the lower body already stone, the looking still a woman’s. Two tiny daughters as ink specks. At most ONE translucent grey wash on the stone. FULL-BLEED, no paper margin. No text. No seal. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = chisul. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.
